findings.problem: The interjection enqueue accepts a request that omits the message body and reports success, but the resulting record is UNREADABLE and UNDECIDABLE. The mailbox reader validates each record through the message-shape check, which requires a string `content`; the queue record built for a body-less request has no `content`, so it is silently dropped from every read. Reproduced with the shipped exports: enqueue without content returns status 'pending', yet the pending read returns 0; the same call WITH content returns 1. Consequently expiry finds nothing (silence never turns into a decision) and a decision on the request throws `interjection "<id>" does not exist`, which misreports a shape problem as a missing record. The existing QA case avoids this only because it happens to pass a `content` field; the shipped docstring does not state that requirement, so a caller following it creates an invisible request — the exact silent-failure class this wave exists to remove. Note the tool-boundary authorization work already declared as out of wave scope is a DIFFERENT gap, not this one.
findings.requiredFix: Pick one and pin it with a test: (a) document `content` as required and reject a body-less request loudly at enqueue with a clear message, or (b) default the body from the summary/reason fields so the record always satisfies the shape check. Also make the decision path distinguish 'record malformed/invisible' from 'id not found', so the current misleading error cannot mask this class again.

residualRisks: The end-to-end delivery after approval (posting the approved request back into the requester's inbox and delivering it at the next step boundary) is explicitly NOT verified by either the implementation or this pass; both record it as an open gap. My evidence covers the request-side safety property (pending requests are never auto-delivered) and the decision RECORD, not the round trip.

The real scheduler idle-edge delivery path was not exercised with spawned members; the safety property is proven at the predicate level on a hand-placed record, which is the strongest available form in an isolated headless environment.

Every headless boot ends on the missing model credential in this environment, so no successful model turn is covered; the mount proof therefore rests on start-up markers plus the absence of abort signatures.
